rules.statement: Don't ask for rewording, rewrapping or reformatting of text that comes from the NCodeGroup project template (files under `.template/` and template-merged sections of files such as `.editorconfig`); if the change is wanted, it belongs upstream in the template.
rules.why: Every template update replaces `.template/` and merges the template-owned files, so editing that text in one project only makes the copy drift from the template.
rules.check: Before reporting a style issue in `.template/**` or in a template-merged section of `.editorconfig` or another shared config file, check whether the text matches the template's. If it does, don't report it in the project.

rules.statement: Don't report comments for being longer than a column width unless a repository instruction sets a wrap width, and the file doesn't already have many long single-line comments.
rules.why: No NCodeGroup convention asks for comments wrapped at 120 columns, and long single-line comments are already normal in these files.
rules.check: Look in AGENTS.md, `.github/instructions/`, `.claude/rules/` and `docs/decisions/` for a comment-width rule, and look at the line lengths of existing comments in the file, before raising a wrap finding.

rules.statement: Don't ask for an analyzer suppression comment in `.editorconfig` to name a tracking issue, a decision record or a removal condition. A one-line reason is all the conventions require, especially for a permanent exemption scoped to generated files.
rules.why: The test conventions ask only for a one-line reason when a rule is turned off. An exemption that covers only a generated file, such as xunit's `XunitAutoGeneratedEntryPoint.cs`, isn't a temporary workaround, and the project's own code still keeps the rule.
rules.check: Check whether the `.editorconfig` section that disables the rule has a comment giving a reason, and whether its glob covers only generated files. If both hold, don't raise a finding.

rules.statement: Don't ask a template-update pull request's description to list behavior that came in with the upstream template, such as new `Update-Project.ps1` features. The template's changelog documents those changes, and the description summarizes only the project's own side.
rules.why: Behavior from the template is already described upstream under the template's issue. Also, the automated feedback run edits a description only to add `Closes` lines, so no commit can answer such a finding.
rules.check: Before reporting something missing from a pull request description, check whether the change is in template-owned files and the template's changelog describes it. If so, don't report it.
